claim: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with m=min D, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=2+min{1/8,1/m}, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with m=min D, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=2+min{1/8,1/m}, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.
quadruple.stage: Finite base-labelled pure-power supplies in the nonnegative integers, with numerical finite-sum sets and finite-dimensional torus phases.

shape.objects: Universally quantified finite sets D of distinct integer bases and infinite locally finite label supplies (d,j), plus finite representing supports; finite-support union is an actual amplification operation when a disjoint bounded-gap reserve and a sufficiently long interval are given. A complete library inventory for the auxiliary Bohr definitions is unknown.
shape.quantifiers: For every admissible finite D, every integer k>=1 and finite deletion F, there exists N(D,k,F), for every n>=N there exists a finite legal representing support. These are countable arithmetic inputs, not universal quantification over arbitrary sets of reals; the prospective Bohr witnesses are existential.
shape.target_quantity: Eventual representability, a yes/no existence property at the fixed explicit sufficient mass2+min{1/8,1/m}; not an optimal numeric value or an upper bound on a density. An unspecified finite N(D,k,F) suffices, but the stated mass endpoint may not weaken.
shape.ambient_structure: Integer order, finite-support capacity, arithmetic gcd, and torus phases coexist. Union on disjoint supports and the accepted interval-plus-syndetic-reserve operation are valid; Bohr correction uses a compact torus. No density-increment piece system or controlled probabilistic pairwise-dependence parameter has been established.
shape.symmetries: Base relabelling and label-preserving representation unions are allowed. Arbitrary translation, mixed-base multiplication, intersection and dilation are not preservation operations for the whole pure-power configuration.
shape.configuration: The required relation is n=sum_{(d,j) in H}d^j on one finite set H of available labels, each used at most once. Base restriction may destroy the reciprocal mass or gcd; truncation may remove a proposed finite interval. It is a positive representation relation, not avoidance of an additive configuration.
shape.finite_certificates: For a fixed input a finite represented interval and a proved disjoint reserve-gap bound constitute a checkable sufficient certificate; no bound on its search scale is known for every input. The full instance quantifies over an infinite tail, and there is no finite global root certificate or reviewed finite experiment.
shape.monotonicity: Adding available labels preserves representation. Raising the sufficient reciprocal-mass threshold restricts the input domain, and lowering the positive cutoff adds labels. The original smallest positive cutoff is one; no finite maximal base range is sufficient.
shape.uniformity_parameter: All finite D, arbitrary positive cutoffs k, arbitrary finite deletions F, and unbounded target integers; N may depend on D,k,F. The OC or WOC Bohr dimension and open set may depend on its supply and cutoff.
shape.proof_shape: The analytical candidates in moves/001-oc-conditional-bridge.md and moves/002-woc-restricted-bridge.md prove the exact admitted high-mass conclusion conditionally on OC and then on its domain-restricted WOC form. The finite core, phase correction and disjoint reserve are unconditional inherited lemmas. The result remains an implication, not the unconditional claim.
shape.neighbours: Known local theorems: high mass3+min{1/4,2/m}, minimum-three11/6, and the common-radix reserve criterion. Known published analogue: the sum of two syndetic sets is piecewise Bohr (Bergelson-Simmons Lemma2.12); Delta-star sets give strongly piecewise Bohr-zero sets (Host-Kra Theorem2.8). Open here: one-class OC and proposed restricted WOC, the full lower-threshold target, and its complement towards mass one. Generic surplus and signed-tail seed strengthenings have accepted counterexamples. No verbatim simpler ambient or property-reflecting correspondence to another category is established, and no uncountable independence or countable/definable contrast is recorded.
shape.known_bounds: Accepted thresholds are3+min{1/4,2/m} and the named structural special cases; these exclude portions of any possible counterexample domain, including all min-three inputs of the present target. The two-supply finite-correction method stops short of the proposed2+min{1/8,1/m} threshold when only one Bohr supply is available. Core bounds [1,9/8) and [1,1+1/m) occur in accepted proof artifacts. No equivalence of OC or WOC with the target is recorded; no finite residue, uniform bound on N over D,k,F, direct-invariant ceiling, density-increment barrier, first-moment estimate, or certified numerical optimum is established.
shape.missing_input: The sole remaining input for the candidate exact conditional bridge is WOC: every finite base set E>=4 with sigma(E)>1 has a nonempty finite-dimensional piecewise-Bohr positive finite-sum subset at every positive cutoff, with U meeting the integer orbit closure and J positive thick. Move2 removes explicit finite deletion by raising the cutoff beyond all deleted exponents. WOC and the original stronger OC remain unproved arithmetic hypotheses.
shape.base_theory: Ordinary classical mathematics with choice, formalizable in the usual Lean standard axioms for its elementary objects. OC and WOC are arithmetic/compact-group statements within this theory, not extra set-theoretic axioms. No independence or guessing principle is asserted; any later machine check requires a separately reviewed controlled verification and standard-axiom audit.
